findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1918 is 'Arista Networks Telemetry For Splunk' (aristanetworks), an app, not a Splunk_TA_arista add-on, and nothing shows it emits arista:eos:version.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for Arista Networks** (**Splunk_TA_arista**, Splunkbase 1918) for **`arista:eos:version`**
findings.suggested_fix: Name 1918 correctly and state the actual collection path for EOS show version JSON (e.g. REST API Modular Input 1546 against eAPI) with the sourcetype you assign.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1897 is the deprecated 'Cisco ACI Add-on for Splunk Enterprise' whose listing directs users to migrate to Cisco DC Networking (7777); the UC presents it as a current integration producing a cisco:aci:firmware sourcetype not listed anywhere in the guide.
findings.quote: **Cisco ACI Splunk Integration** ([Splunkbase 1897](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1897)) for APIC firmware MO ingestion into **`cisco:aci:firmware`**
findings.suggested_fix: Point to the current Cisco DC Networking app (7777) or a REST collector for the firmware classes, and label cisco:aci:firmware as a custom sourcetype.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation gives Nexus=6876 and Arista=4291 while app gives Nexus=1917 and Arista=1918; the cached catalogue lists 6876 as 'Network Monitoring App', and 1917/4291 are not in the catalogue, so a reader cannot tell which to install.
findings.suggested_fix: Look up the real Splunkbase IDs for the Nexus and Arista collection paths and use the same IDs in app and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: No 'Splunk Add-on for SDN Inventory' appears in the cached Splunkbase catalogue; it looks invented, and detailedImplementation repeats it as an existing product.
findings.quote: optional Splunk Add-on for SDN Inventory patterns where deployments standardize **`fabric_id`** keys across vendors
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the reference unless a real Splunkbase listing can be cited.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Juniper parses Junos syslog/structured syslog; it is not known to collect NETCONF software-runtime snapshots or emit juniper:junos:software, and its package folder name should be confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Splunk Add-on for Juniper documentation for its folder name and sourcetypes; describe juniper:junos:software as a custom NETCONF/REST collector output if that is the real path.

findings.explanation: The SPL only searches cisco:aci:firmware, cisco:nxos:version, arista:eos:version and juniper:junos:software, so SONiC, Cumulus, gNMI and syslog lanes described as part of the detection (and in the 'multi-vendor' title) are never evaluated.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark these lanes as future extensions that require adding the sourcetypes to the base search, or drop them from dataSources.

findings.explanation: These API paths do not match the documented SONiC management REST or NVIDIA NetQ API path conventions and look guessed.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify against SONiC mgmt-framework REST docs and the NVIDIA NetQ API reference and replace with documented endpoints.

findings.explanation: Large parts of Steps 5–6 and the governance annex are generated filler (e.g. 'Sev-2 remains risk-to-life for EoL proximity', ITSI episode_density slopes, SOAR soak timers) that a reader cannot act on and that is not tied to the SPL; it also contains typos such as 'isuu_capable'.
findings.quote: Subscribe vendor field-notice CSV bridges enriching **serial_number** rows with thermal FPGA notices adjunct to upgrades yet unrelated logically.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut Steps 5–6 and the annex to concrete enrichment (EOX lookup by serial, wave calendar maintenance) and alert thresholds that match the SPL.

findings.explanation: fabric_compliance_pct is a per-fabric value, so averaging it by role×vendor is meaningless (role_compliance_pct is the per-role metric), and the SPL covers 24h with no _time output, so a 30-day trend needs a summary index not described.
findings.quote: (4) Heat matrix — **`role`** (leaf / spine / edge) × **`vendor`** showing average **`fabric_compliance_pct`**. (5) Timechart — trailing thirty-day **`fabric_compliance_pct`** trend
findings.suggested_fix: Use role_compliance_pct for the matrix and state that the trend panel reads a daily summary-indexed copy of the result.

findings.explanation: The DX010 (Seastone) SONiC reference switch is a Celestica platform, not Edgecore.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'Celestica DX010' or name an actual Edgecore SONiC model.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by an automated reviewer despite conflicting Splunkbase IDs and invented add-ons.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME validates.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: target_version is built with trim(coalesce(...,"")), so it is never null and `isnotnull(target_version)` is always true. Devices with no target get on_target=1 only when os_version is also empty, and otherwise straggler_flag=1 because a lookup miss defaults wave_start_ts to now-31d (wave_age_days=31>30). Every device not in fabric_wave_calendar is therefore reported as a Straggler. Test `target_version!=""` instead.

T1542.005 is 'Pre-OS Boot: TFTP Boot' (adversary boots a malicious network image). This UC compares running OS versions to an approved wave target and EoL dates; it does not detect TFTP/netboot of unauthorized images, so the tag overstates ATT&CK coverage.

summary: The wave/straggler/EoL compliance concept is valuable and the grandma text is excellent, but Splunkbase IDs and add-on names contradict the catalogue and each other, the SPL treats empty target_version as present (so unmapped devices become stragglers), the data sources promise lanes the SPL never reads, and the ATT&CK tag does not fit.
